corpus.kind: deterministic synthetic sequences (NOT a curriculum, NOT language)

findings.1_replay_is_a_uniform_translation_not_se: with a constant lr and reward 0, every visited pair gains the same amount per pass, so replay cannot strengthen one engram relative to another. After 3 cycles mean == max == min: the chain has one value.
findings.2_past_the_ceiling_replay_destroys_the_r: every entry reaches the 4.0 ceiling at pass 9; at that point all pairs are equal, so the within-slot ordering generate() reads through SUCCESSOR_FLOOR/MARGIN is gone. A pass-count limit is a precondition of option A, not an optimisation of it.
findings.3_replay_contaminates_the_organ_s_own_ac: transitions and sequences_learned advance as though new material arrived, and they saturate non-linearly (once nothing grows, `grew` is False and written stops counting), so the drift hides itself in the counters that published evidence quotes.
findings.4_consequence_for_the_ruling: option A costs no code and cannot express selective consolidation; option B (a dedicated replay entry with a replay gain, advancing no teaching counter) is the only one that can, and it is an organ change. See docs/mp_e10_g3_decision_brief.md.
